$description: Web experience density. Emitted as CSS variables in generated web.css.

typography.$description: Chrome typography roles (#1216). A role names the text's job and owns the coherent size / weight / leading treatment for that job at Web density. Family (product sans vs technical mono) stays with the text's meaning at the call site — a path is mono at the code role's metrics, not mono because the role is smaller. Workload renderers (xterm, CodeMirror, Markdown document prose) stay on their own surfaces.

title.$description: The surface's own name when Web chrome renders a page header or pushed detail title.

primary.$description: Work / local primary — highest within its region. Session name, active file, focused input.

body.$description: Ordinary readable product text and controls — button labels, menu items, filters.

secondary.$description: Supporting but fully readable. Section headings, tree rows, infrastructure rows.

metadata.$description: Quiet factual context. Agent/location, recency, status details — never outweighs the thing it describes.

caption.$description: Lowest deliberate readable hierarchy — keyboard hints, tiny helper copy, sidebar service state.

code.$description: Chrome-side technical identity — paths, commands, env keys. Not xterm/CodeMirror workload glyphs.

visualSize.$description: The affordance actually painted inside a control — the circle a capsule icon action draws — as opposed to the box that receives the tap. Equal to `control.md` (32px) by construction: a pointer has no minimum hit area, so on Web the drawn affordance may fill the control it sits in and the split is a no-op. The leaf exists so a single shared binding resolves on both experiences — an App-only token would be written into [data-experience=app] only and resolve to nothing at `:root` — and so the drawn-affordance check can be stated once against both. See the App side for where the two deliberately differ.

sidebarWidth.$description: Expanded sidebar column. The mockup draws 246px; the shell's grid is `246px 1fr`.

sessionRowPadY.$description: Session row vertical padding. The mockup draws 7px, tighter than `shell.space-2` (8px) because the row's two lines already carry leading; horizontal padding is `shell.space-2`.

sessionRowRadius.$description: Sidebar list row corner radius, shared by session rows and agent/node rows. The mockup rounds the row so the selected `--n-raised` fill reads as a chip rather than a band.

nodeRowPadY.$description: Agent/node row vertical padding. The mockup draws 6px — tighter than a session row's 7px, because a node row carries one line where a session row carries two.

nodeFontSize.$description: Agent/node row text — the secondary role at Web density (#1216). Product face: a node row is infrastructure context (a name and a count), not technical workload identity (#1050 stage 4).

sessionRowTitleFontSize.$description: Session name — the sidebar's primary role. The mockup's 12.5px, a half step below `text-sm` so two lines plus padding fit the row.

sessionRowMetaFontSize.$description: Session metadata (agent / recency) — the metadata role. A full step below the title, so the title leads and the metadata never outweighs the thing it describes (visual-language.md typography rules). Family is per slot since #1050 stage 4: the line's workload slot is the pane's foreground command, so it keeps monospace, while the node name and the recency are the metadata role's own "Agent/location, recency" and are set in the product face. The size is shared by all three because a role owns size, not family.

footPadY.$description: Sidebar foot vertical padding. The mockup draws 9px; horizontal is `shell.space-3` (12px), which is what the mockup draws too.

footGap.$description: Sidebar foot gap between the status dot, its text and the controls.

statusDotSize.$description: The sidebar's status mark, shared by the foot's service dot, the collapsed rail's and the agent/node rows — one object in three places. Small on purpose: the mockup's comment on the foot is 'Healthy stays quiet; degraded may gain emphasis', so a steady state is a 5px mark beside quiet text rather than a badge.

footFontSize.$description: Sidebar foot text — the caption role (#1216). A service state and a node count: quiet infrastructure chrome, not session metadata.

sectionHeadFontSize.$description: Sidebar section label (Agents / Sessions) — the secondary role. Muted and below `text-xs`, so a section label never competes with the rows it names. Top padding is `shell.space-1` (4px) and the sides `shell.space-2` (8px), which is what the mockup draws.

sectionHeadPadBottom.$description: Sidebar section label bottom padding. The mockup draws 7px, tighter than the sides so the label sits with the rows it names rather than floating between sections.

sectionSepMargin.$description: Inset separator between sidebar sections. The mockup draws `margin: 8px`, so the rule does not run edge to edge — it reads as a division inside the column, not as another panel edge.

terminal.$description: The Web work surface's own typography and inset. terminal-surface.md §Resize and typography: 'font/scrollback/control metrics come from Experience tokens, not ad-hoc breakpoint values' — until this group existed the xterm boundary read hardcoded 14px / line-height 1.2 literals that no token owned. The mockup's `.term` draws `font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.62; padding: 18px 18px 52px`. Two channels, because xterm is a canvas renderer: the inset is CSS (`--terminal-pad-*`), the font metrics are xterm options read from `TERMINAL_METRICS` in `design/generated/terminal.ts` — xterm takes a JS object, which is the same reason the ANSI theme is emitted there. The mockup's third padding value is deliberately NOT a token: 52px is the capsule's own box (14px bottom margin + 36px capsule + 2), i.e. the clearance `--terminal-content-bottom-inset` already measures, and freezing it would reserve fixed space for chrome that may not be drawn — terminal-surface.md's 'shrink the terminal grid with large fixed padding to reserve hypothetical UI'. Deliberately not a ref to `typography.primary.size`: visual-language.md keeps terminal glyph rendering separate from chrome typography even where the sizes coincide.

lineHeight.$description: Converted, not transcribed — because the unit differs. The mockup's CSS `line-height: 1.62` multiplies the *font size*: 12.5px × 1.62 = a 20.25px line box. xterm's `lineHeight` multiplies the font's *measured box* instead, which for JetBrains Mono is 1.36em — 17px at 12.5px. Handing xterm the mockup's raw `1.62` therefore draws a 27px row, 33% looser than the mockup, so the number that reproduces the mockup's leading is 20.25 ÷ 17 = 1.19. The target is the mockup's *appearance*; its literal number means something else in this unit, and copying it would have been the divergence.

capabilitySlotWidth.$description: Fixed slot for one capability entry in the Workspace capsule. The bound is what keeps a long label (Claude Code) from widening the row: the slot stays this wide and the label wraps inside it instead (#1347 follow-up).

capabilityEntryHeight.$description: One labeled capability entry's height on Web. Deliberately above `control-md` (32px): the entry stacks icon over label, and this is the band where the pair fits without crowding — 40px of entry in the pill's 6px shell pad, against the Web composer's 32px row. A floor, not a cap: a two-line label grows the entry by its own line box rather than clipping.

capabilityLabelFontSize.$description: Capability entry label, one line. The entry reads icon-over-label; a label that fits one line gets this size.

capabilityLabelWrappedFontSize.$description: Capability entry label, two lines. Same slot, smaller type — a wrapped label at the one-line size would crowd the icon and outweigh its neighbours (#1347 follow-up). The entry picks between the two by its own measured line count.

projectionMarginBottom.$description: Gap between an emerged projection and the capsule below it. Close enough to read as attached to it, far enough that the two surfaces do not merge.

projectionMaxHeight.$description: Ceiling for an emerged projection (#826 Q5). It is a small surface floating over the work, so it stops well short of the terminal and scrolls its own overflow rather than taking the viewport's.

projectionFontSize.$description: One step below the capsule's own scale. The Peek draws the smallest identifying state, not the composer's text, so it must not arrive at the field's size.

projectionMarkWidth.$description: The change letter's column (M/A/D/?) in a compact listing. Fixed so the filenames beside it share a left edge.

marginBottom.$description: The inter-Capsule gap: the deliberate space between the upper Context Capsule and the resting Conversation Capsule below it (#1347 SC-43). The same value as projectionMarginBottom so a list-to-Peek swap does not jump the gap, but a separate leaf because the two pairs may diverge — a Peek is read while typing, the list is a place you stop.

maxHeight.$description: Ceiling for the upper Context Capsule (#1347 SC-44). The surface takes its content's natural height and only clamps here, so a short list is short instead of reserving room for rows that do not exist; content beyond the ceiling scrolls inside it. A ceiling rather than a height because the flat list renders every capability, so quiet, working and context-only differ in row ORDER and never in row COUNT — the pair still does not resize as senses come and go, which is the stability a fixed height was protecting, but it now comes from the list's own invariant rather than from a box. Equal to this experience's projectionMaxHeight, so deepening the list into a Peek can reach the same ceiling, and the region above this dock has already been proven to hold that much.

rowHeight.$description: One capability row in the Context Capsule: capability icon, title, and one line of reason for a sensed capability (#1347 SC-19/SC-42). 44px on both experiences — two lines of text need at least 40, and on App this is exactly the touch floor, so a row is a legal App target by construction.

markerSize.$description: The presence mark beside an ordinary row's title: a capability the session actually needs. The same 5px as the shell's status dot on purpose — both are 'a quiet mark beside text' rather than a badge — but a separate leaf, because that one answers service health while this answers capability presence, and the design system's rule is that an equal resolved value does not make two names interchangeable.

conversation.$description: Web density for an AI conversation transcript (#1363). The rhythm is the design: work rows sit close together so a long process reads as one block, and the answer is separated from that block by the loose gap so it reads as the thing you came for. Only the measurements live here — the hierarchy that motivates them is owned by the pattern doc.

rowGap.$description: Between two rows of the same process group. Tight, because a group is scanned as one unit rather than read.

rowGapExpanded.$description: Between rows of a group the reader has opened. Looser, because now each row is being read on its own.

responseGap.$description: Between blocks of one assistant response. Looser than a process row gap: this is the content, and its parts should not run together.

turnGap.$description: Between a turn's own parts — the process control, the answer, the actions.

processToAnswerGap.$description: From a collapsed process control to the answer it precedes. Tighter than `turnGap`, because a folded process is a label for the answer rather than a peer of it.

groupTitleGap.$description: Below an expanded group's title — the space that says the title belongs to the body rather than to the next title.

groupMaxHeight.$description: Cap on a process group's body before it scrolls inside itself. Viewport-relative as well as absolute: a group on a short window must not push its own answer off screen.

groupFade.$description: The edge fade that says a capped group body continues past the cap — the affordance, since a scrollbar gutter may be hidden.

readingColumnMax.$description: The measure for assistant prose. Replaces the ad-hoc `max-w-prose` the transcript used before #1363: a readable line length is a conversation decision, and stating it here is what lets App state its own.

bubbleMaxWidth.$description: The user's bubble as a fraction of the reading column — deliberately well under it, so a short prompt is a short bubble and the assistant's answer owns the full measure. App states the wider value.

foldControlHeight.$description: The one-line process control. Its own height rather than a control token's, because it is a text row with a hairline under it rather than a button with a box.

workspace.$description: Web Workspace master/detail. The mockup draws the tree at a fixed 208px — a navigation column sized to its content, not a fraction of the pane — with the editor taking the rest.

treeFontSize.$description: Tree text — the secondary role. Monospace: a path is workload identity, and the mockup sets the whole tree in mono rather than only the filenames.

treeLineHeight.$description: Tree line box. Looser than the text size implies, which is what lets the row's own vertical padding stay at 1px and still scan as a list.

treeRowPadY.$description: Tree row vertical padding. 1px, because `lineHeight: 1.85` already carries the row's breathing room — padding and leading together would double it.

treeIndentStep.$description: Indent per tree depth. The mockup's levels are 20/33/46px from a 7px row inset, i.e. 13px a step.

editorFontSize.$description: The code surface — the code role. Terminal glyph rendering stays with the terminal; this is chrome-side code text.

editorLineHeight.$description: Code line box. The mockup's 1.75, looser than the tree's 1.85 ratio at a larger size — line numbers have to line up with their line.

editorGutterWidth.$description: Line-number column. Fixed so numbers align regardless of digit count.

editorPadY.$description: Code surface vertical padding. The mockup's 14px, top and bottom, so the first line is not flush against the header.

editorGutterPadEnd.$description: Space between the line numbers and the code. The mockup's 14px — wide enough that a number and the first glyph do not read as one token.

envProfileTitleFontSize.$description: Environment profile detail/editor page title — the title role (#1216). Bridges the role into workspace chrome tokens so the ref graph reaches production consumers.

editorHeadFontSize.$description: The file path above the code. Muted and below `text-xs`: it names what is open, it is not a title competing with the work.

listRowTitleFontSize.$description: A file/directory row's own name — the `text-sm` literal `FileList` used to carry. It is stated here as well as on App (#1073) because one class serves both: the leaf exists so the class resolves either way, and an App-only leaf would be dropped silently at `:root`. Not a ref to `typography.primary.size`: this is Web's desktop row size, and the size in the App's scale is the App group's business. `FileList` is composed by `FilesAppLayout` today, so this leaf's App value is the one that reaches a screen — the Web value is the fallback the shared class needs, not a claim about a Web surface that renders it.

editorActionFontSize.$description: The viewer toolbar's own controls (Edit / Save / View / Raw / close) — the body role (#1216). Stated on both experiences for the same reason as `listRowTitleFontSize`: `FileViewer` is composed by both layouts, so the leaf has one consumer class and two densities (#1073).

editorHeadPadX.$description: Header horizontal inset. The mockup's 18px, which is wider than the shell's `space-4` — the header is inside the code surface, so it aligns to the code's own measure rather than to the pane's chrome padding.
